motion: Palestinians risk becoming their own worst enemy

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: Your word 'protection' does the least work here. Warning about internal failures may be useful, but calling Palestinians their own worst enemy erases far greater forces harming them.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: Sarah, if leaders suppress warnings that protect civilians, why should Palestinians pretend the damage is only external? Isn't naming that danger necessary to prevent them becoming their own worst enemy?

turns.speaker: CON

turns.speaker: CON

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: On your 'criticism is betrayal' point, Palestinians do argue, organize, and challenge leaders. You assume internal disagreement proves collective self-sabotage, but it proves a society refusing silence.

turns.text: When local leaders silence peaceful critics, Palestinians risk weakening the unity and judgment they need. In that specific situation, refusing honest correction can make them their own worst enemy.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: People also need schools, work, and room to grieve, not constant arguments over slogans. Those needs show why reducing Palestinians to their leaders is wrong; they are not their own worst enemy.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Ordinary families are not identical to their leaders, and I accept that distinction. Yet the motion warns of a risk: silencing those families' criticism lets destructive leadership damage their future.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Your 'risk' claim is so broad that any oppressed community could be blamed for harms done to it. A possibility is not proof that Palestinians are their own worst enemy.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: People facing oppression need internal debate as much as they need solidarity. A movement that protects dissent is stronger; when it abandons that principle, it risks serving its people badly.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Your 'internal debate' point actually undermines you: debate exists because Palestinians are not marching blindly toward self-destruction. You turn a safeguard into evidence of the danger you claim.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Imagine a neighborhood committee warning that a planned attack will bring retaliation on nearby families, then being threatened into silence. The harm falls on Palestinians first, proving the risk is real.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I reject the premise that a threatened committee represents Palestinians as a people. Your example condemns coercion, but it cannot show that the community resisting coercion is its own worst enemy.
